Couple things to add to this conversation on some possibilities as to why some do better on dairy than others....

1. 90% of cheese made in the U.S. is either a Pfizer mold based processed rennet or vegetable enzymes.
So, if you are sensitive to mold or oxylates, eating cheese thats not made from animal rennet might be an issue.

2. Milk products. There's two types of milk, A1 & A2. Most milk products are made with A1. 
"A1 milk contains the amino acid histidine at position 67, while A2 contains proline. This tiny change affects digestion and how your body reacts to the dairy."

3. Butter. Most brands are a combination of A1 milk and seed oils they dont list on the label. So, sensitive tummys might have a problem. 
The safest butter is Kerry Gold.

Lastly, let's not forget many of these heavy creams have questionable ingredients like polysorbate 80 and carrageene.

So, if you question any of these, read your labels. Dont buy products with questionable ingredients. Contact the manufacturer and inquire. Its the only way to know.

PS..

If a dairy company uses hoilstein cows, they produce A1 milk. 
If they have jersey or Guernsey, its A2.
